title: Token-level visual-sensitivity steering as a hallucination monitor for small VLMs

original_idea.body: Compute a per-token visual-sensitivity score on a small open VLM and test whether low-sensitivity tokens predict hallucinated content, building a token-level flag.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Multimodal hallucination is a real harm but the chain to catastrophic risk from advanced AI is moderate/indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Per-token VLM activation-difference analysis requires solid ML fundamentals and multimodal tooling; intermediate.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (token-level flag) but VLM activation extraction + labeling hallucinated tokens has dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Read-only monitor reframing, open VLM, no internal access; multimodal monitoring is externally doable.

low_compute.reasoning: Small VLM inference fits one GPU but multimodal models are heavier; single GPU days.

novelty.reasoning: Reframing visual-sensitivity steering as a read-only hallucination detector appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Using the visual-sensitivity signal as a read-only per-token hallucination detector is an underexplored reframing.
